hook: Saturn reaches opposition on October 4, 2026, shining in the constellation Cetus at magnitude 0.3.

sections.voiceover: Saturn reaches opposition on October 4, 2026, shining in the constellation Cetus at magnitude 0.3.
sections.visual_cue: Wide cosmic shot of Saturn glowing brightly against the dark starry void of Cetus.
sections.sfx_cue: Deep space drone and a resonant chime.
b_roll: Astrophotography still of Saturn in Cetus
sections.animation_cue: Fade in from black with a slow cinematic zoom.

sections.voiceover: On October 4, 2026, at 8 A.M. EDT, Saturn reaches opposition. The planet exhibits a 19.7-arcsecond disk with rings tilted 7.5 degrees toward Earth. Where will Jupiter hide just two days later?
sections.visual_cue: Orbital diagram showing Earth and Saturn aligned opposite the Sun.
b_roll: Telescopic view of Saturn disk and ring tilt
sections.animation_cue: Panned orbit lines scaling up smoothly.
sections.transition_out: Pan across to the Moon and Jupiter.

sections.voiceover: Except Saturn is only part of October's rare celestial alignment.
sections.visual_cue: Camera sweeps past Saturn toward the glowing limb of the waning crescent Moon.

sections.voiceover: On October 6, 2026, a waning crescent Moon occults Jupiter as seen from New York, USA. Observers witness the gas giant vanish behind the lunar limb completely.
sections.visual_cue: Close up simulation of the Moon sliding directly across the bright disk of Jupiter over New York.
b_roll: Astronomy simulation of lunar occultation over New York

sections.voiceover: Magnitude 0.3 light travels across the solar system to meet us.
sections.visual_cue: Slow cinematic pull back from Saturn into the vast expanse of the cosmos.
sections.animation_cue: Slow steady zoom out to infinity.
